A reimagining of Zobros' "Ultimate Demon Mix", often containing fast-paced gameplay requiring a variety of skillsets. Each part of the level is styled after one of 23 different demons.

Kinetic Bypass is a fast, skill-based 2.1 design level by Sminx and verified by Luqualizer. Despite its shorter length, it uses a wide variety of gameplay styles; featuring a slow predrop, wave, robot, a long dual, and flow gameplay.
The sequel to the Insane Demon Apache, featuring blinding decoration with an extremely intense song. Started in 2018 and was reworked multiple times.
2.1 click sync megacollab, known for its low CPS. Much of the level is a dual, and the ending is difficult and nerve-wracking. Named after the Greek god of deception.
A Classic styled xSlendy level seemingly inspired by Saul Goodman. Startpos: 120275555

Hack-verified level from 2016 which includes very difficult wave chokepoints, including an infamously difficult dual wave at 70%. It is one of the many hell-themed top 1s, surpassing Sakupen Hell when it was placed.

Incredibly creative and unpolished extreme with alternative memory gameplay and extremely chaotic decoration, both of which inspired by Toxin Lab III. Features a difficult wave maze and an intimidating predrop. Despite its quirks, the gameplay is very highly regarded among victors!
Early 2.1 timing and nerve control level notable due to numerous chokepoints throughout the level, most noteworthy being the 'pants-shittingly' difficult ending segment by Lemons.
A 2-player level, a part of the gang trilogy. The level's name is meant to be a British version of Based Gang. Has a key you can collect to turn the bossfight icons into the Bass Cave demon.
Shmigels solo level featuring intentionally wacky gameplay. Has an infamous last ship, and the asymmetrical dual is featured in BarbarosFinaleFinale with added camera effects.

A highly click-sync based megacollab. While the gameplay aligns with the music, its gimmicky nature still requires memorization and practice. The decoration is colorful and energetic, reflecting the fast-paced song. The layout showcase, "highscore w/ clicks", managed to get over 3M views.

Legendary extreme demon with a very rich history. The original version created by Hota1991 had around a million objects, the most out of any level of its time. Because of how laggy the level was for most people, Stilluetto created an nerfed optimized version, cutting the object count in half. The original version was rated twice on accident, once in 2023 and again in 2026 right before the optimized version got rated. The level is split into nine parts, each exploring a different part of hell.

Glitchy & hyper-dense solo 1.9 styled level about what the level's name suggests. Memorable for its fun, unconventional memory gameplay and claustrophobic structuring that might appear as object spam at first.

Solo extreme themed around diseased and decomposing flesh, with fast paced and generally well received gameplay, and strong music representation. Most notably has a very confusing and unusually structured timing based predrop. The previous description was way too funny so I'm leaving it in: "Loltad level with a very unique and interesting theme, paired with very unique and interesting gameplay."
Relatively unknown Korean duo level notable for its extremely fast-paced dual gameplay. Contains neo-design adjacent decoration with an inconsistent pink and blue palette.

Newgrounds-themed level with a gray and orange color scheme, and uses elements of the site such as bits of text, a big angry emoji, and tankmen to compliment the Newgrounds style. Known for its iconic song which disses BrokenDeck, and the drop parts using unique spider timings.
An  ice-themed remaster of Sakupen Hell, containing the same gameplay with some alterations, including the addition of a difficult wave extension and a chokable cube section near the end.
An extremely large megacollab of 193 people, hosted by Akunakun, where each creator has a 3 block long part. The gameplay is corridor based.
Known for being a robbed top 1 and taking nearly 9 years to finally get rated. Infamous for it's wave at around half way through the level.

Solo created and verified 2-player level made for Lia's and Gecko's 2P Creator Contest, using a song from a Persona 4 spin-off game. The gameplay is entirely clicksync and very learny. The drop, from 33%-42%, is by far the hardest part.
Forgotten sequel to Cataclysm. Hack verified like its predecessor. Infamous for a really difficult UFO at 65%, and a difficult coin at the last ship.
An open ended solo level that is intended to run alongside vRidge's other extreme To The Blue Moon.
Solo intended XL 2p level by Bram4Real, inspired by his own experience in trail hiking. The level has hard timing gameplay for the predrop and drop, and then turns into a 2p dual for the rest.

2 player extreme where one player has to perform standard gameplay as the other player clicks in a repetitive pattern, matching the rhythm of the 'wobbling' technique in Smash Bros. Melee. Originally hack verified and unrated, but later nerfed and re-verified after which it took over two years to get re-rated.

stcubing's first megacollab, birthed from a Cognition/Oblivion spinoff layout created out of spite for Carcano. It features bright colours and decoration with an upbeat song, and is one of the more accessible levels of this genre.

A 2-player level that takes inspiration from Bang Gang. In order to make it more feasible to do solo, the final 20% can be nerfed in exchange for not getting the coin. Despite this, it's still the hardest part of the level when done solo.
A remake of the 1.9 level MadHouse, with a grayscale color palette and subtle hints of other hues. Like the original, it is heavily memory-based and uses the same song.

A short and fast paced ATOMIC CANNON inspired solo level by AREDL list leader Shyne! Features names of many AREDL members throughout, a horizontal spider orb, and has an infamously hard wave near the end. Has become a large insider meme in AREDL, and additionally took 6 months and 33 opinions to place on NLW...
XL solo extreme featuring clean sky themed decoration and click sync gameplay

The first 2-player extreme in Geometry Dash. Was verified by four different people swapping positions mid-completion. The decoration is in DanZmeN's typicial 2019 style. Features learny segments and a bossfight with arrows that are not entirely accurate. The first victor, Grey479 is also the verifier for the level's solo completion, with them being awarded $3,000 AUD for it.
Dense & colorful memory "insane demon" created by the feared memory creator Akunakun and verified by the beloved youtuber Tride. Includes 12 large, distinct, and extremely confusing mazes.
DanZmeN level with a goated song, overall is extremely fun, but can feel frustrating due to balancing issues, with waves being the primary difficulty of the level. The ending is terrifying.

2.1 remake of Andromeda's infamous insane demon. While generally better received than the original, this level remains quite chokepoint heavy. Also features a short extension with a tough memory last wave.

2.1 megacollab hosted by LIEB with a prevalent sky theme throughout, infamous for Tob's steampunk themed part and the tight waves at the beginning of the drop. Despite being considered quite first-half heavy and having several blind clicks, it's still received positively by its victors

An extremely high quality 2.0 level by two of the most talented creators at the time. Features multiple iconic parts such as the black hole UFO and asymmetrical dual, and is generally harder at the start and end. Formerly an upcoming top 1 before receiving a large nerfdate making it more accessible and enjoyable. Go up in the ship at 55% to avoid the transition bug!
Tabgnid's first solo level, a 1.9-style extreme with flow gameplay inspired by Prismatic Haze.

A 5 and a half minute level to the tune of the Radiohead song of the same name. It takes on a very progression-based approach to represent its song - the level spends its first half building up to its climax with fast-paced gameplay and flashy visuals before ending off on a much slower 2 minute-long timing-based ending.
An early 2.1 extreme demon that took 8 years to be rated. The gameplay has scattered chokepoints, with the middle of the level being much harder than the rest of the level.
Solo XXL greyscale level themed around exploring a mechanical city, and utilising a vocaloid song to good effect. The gameplay incorporates a lot of moving objects, and has a dual heavy second half

1.9/2.0 megacollab that was initially hack-verified in a much harder state, but was reverified in an easier form by KrmaL. The level doesn't have a very high enjoyment, and contains a lot of difficulty spikes.

Repetition-based memory extreme using a Madeon song and only cube, robot and ball for its gamemodes. It's reminiscent of the Sunset Sandstorm predrop, with deviations between the same repeated pattern to match the song. The 2nd half is a nerve wracking ball section that is very chokable.
A Stormfly megacollab remake of Silent clubstep, containing almost identical gameplay, albeit heavily nerfed.

A short, extremely fast-paced level made up of highly compressed difficulty in its total runtime of 41 seconds. Has very tight wave parts that require precise control, as well as generally high CPS gameplay chockfull with timings galore.

Famous for being the level to take the #1 spot away from Bloodbath. Known to be very imbalanced, with the majority of the difficulty coming from the waves. It's also the shortest former top 1 in terms of level length, with the gameplay lasting under 50 seconds.
A megacollab themed around early 2.1 levels, containing stereotypical decoration and gameplay elements inspired by its reference time period. It took nearly a year for the level to finally get rated.
2.2 Prismatic Haze remake that also doubles as the first Turkish solo extreme demon ever!

A somewhat lesser known 2.0 extreme with skill based gameplay in the first half, which features a relatively difficult mini ball and dual wave section. The second half introduces memory sections including a cube maze that turns invisible towards the end.

Murder Drones themed level with a nightcore-metal song from the final episode. Involves numerous references from the show and many flashy, tech themed effects. Although incredibly learny, the gameplay is highly praised.

The official sequel to Prismatic by CatGeo made by a different creator. The gameplay differs with its faster gameplay and difficult ship parts. The decoration has much more variation in it including a complete tone shift at 64%. 2nd Parfait extreme.
The last Extreme Demon uploaded in 2.1; A colorful, glowy, and vaguely aurora-themed level, described by the creator as a "floating world under the moonlight."
A-
Shiver me timbers, be that an XXL pirate themed megacollab! Yahar matey! (full creator list will be added soon)
The final installment in the Fusion series. An extremely long and intense level with well rounded but stressful gameplay. Has a very long, complex, and controversial history.
Solo XXL+ extreme to the tune of Revolution 1993 by Jamiroquai. Features many dual sections over its 10 minute runtime. Come on, fight the power!

A popular Cognition-style corridor level built by two Polish creators, with high CPS and timing-based gameplay. Despite receiving a nerfdate in early 2022, community opinions are still quite mixed, which wasn't helped by the slope interaction changes in 2.2.

A three minute long non stop memory level. Gets gradually harder as the level progresses, with a very hard wave near the end. Received a balance update in late 2024 which both buffed the first half and nerfed the second half, easing the difficulty increase through the level.

1.9gdps nine circles extreme demon collab made by Jakalope, royen, and valentine that focuses on detail and intense nine circles effects reflecting the song. The gameplay and design is generally praised by most people who've played it.
Effect layout by HHyper, with an iconic bossfight at the end. The gameplay is gimmicky and learny.

A very unorthodox level featuring an abundance of difficult timings in the first section, becoming a high-CPS wave consistency challenge in the second section that tests the player's stamina and spam skill.
A bright and colourful flow level with a lot of orb focused gameplay.

Very complex hexitine level that plays like a puzzle, and includes a difficult mirror section in the middle. The structuring and effects are unique and well-made, but the level is generally poorly received. Contains invisible hitboxes.
Turqoise and cyan colored level with somewhat high cps sync gameplay. The main difficulty comes from the drop. Resembles one of the 'reta' levels to some extent.

Hypno's second solo Extreme Demon project, inspired by the rhythm game Sayonara Wild Hearts. It showcases Hypno's signature gameplay style: learny yet intuitive, focused on unique structuring. Noteworthy for its difficult duals, exceptional song representation and simplistic neon designs.
Highly popular and well received flowy extreme with a simplistic yet pleasing design. Very chokeable, particularly in the wave sections. Features an immediate ship click at the start.
geometry dash map that shmigels created using the level editor

Very flashy solo extreme you'll regret opening the editor on due to the sheer amount of triggers. The difficulty features varied gameplay, with a dual lasting from 65 all the way to the end giving it an easy but chokeable ending.

Official sequel to Moment, arguably improving on the original. Incorporates a green and pink color scheme while retaining a difficulty very similar to its predecessor. Notably was verified in 2021 and rated in late 2025.

One of the most popular extreme demons in the game, and the second level of the Apocalyptic trilogy. This level was known for being the hardest of its time, due to the ship parts being near impossible at the time. Nowadays a pretty tough level, with Michigun's part being arguably the most difficult.

A 55-minute level that features mostly 6-7 star gameplay over its extremely long runtime, with decoration built using 2.2 effects and triggers to avoid a high object count. It changes themes and energy a lot throughout to represent the song, and increases in difficulty during the final 12%.

A generally well-received 2.2 Lit Fuse-esque extreme demon themed around the aesthetics of computation, featuring a range of gimmick and clicksync gameplay. The coin requires you to read mock code in order to understand how to obtain it.
A megacollaboration by 21 creators serving as a mini-tribute to 1.9, featuring multiple callbacks to older levels. The level is fast-paced with glow-style decoration, and is nearly 4 minutes long.

A faithful OMORI-themed megacollab hosted by Blueskii featuring tons of personality and references galore, including hidden cutscenes and a secret epilogue. The player traverses through various environments from the game, meeting friends and foes along the way. Contains spoilers for OMORI.
Super big early 2.0 megacollab with, some say it was even the biggest one (probably). (Verification video was privated/deleted)
Prequel to Snowfall Fiesta. The level features a summer-like song with somewhat inconsistent decoration.
Colorful skill-based extreme using a Metallica song with very high-cps clicksync gameplay. Contains a difficult predrop and an intimidating cube maze at 84%.

Splitscreen two player level with a distinct red and blue scheme in reference to the Doppler Effect. Created and verified by At242 & Latezk in two weeks! Memorable for its tech theme and satisfying clicksync. Currently the most enjoyed two player level.
Incredibly creative extreme inspired by Magic The Gathering, using Blue Zenith by xi as its song. Memorable for its difficult sideways wave among other unique gameplay gimmicks. Glory to Phyrexia
Simplistic crystal cave themed extreme. Majority of the level features convoluted and long misaligned duals.
A 1.9 style memory extreme made by Airz while they were working on Skeletal Shenanigans. Features a very difficult second half.

Another Waterbound solo that now utilizes more gimmicks like the Beach Ball and the Shwave. It includes a randomized Minesweeper pattern at the end that you have to solve in order to hit the right toggle orb at the end. Also has one of the most evil last clicks in any extreme demon in this range.

Fire themed megacollab with a variety of well known creators, using a buffed Shmigels layout. This level also has randomised memory gimmick where a number at 28% tells you how many times to jump at 33%.
It's him...

A solo XXL extreme where you race your friend to the moon! Created for the Zeronium creator contest, this level features four contrasting sections, repetitive sync gameplay, and a lot of character and personality.

Solo intended 2p extreme by Snoozzzing. This level was made as three separate levels, eventually combined into one. The level is about their experience with suicidal ideation and perseverance. The decoration was inspired by sink and 5ta1ker.
An extremely well known and influential clicksync wave/timing level. Has some very narrow but well synced wave parts, and a slow but very hard ending. Beware of the fish...
A joyous remake of the famous extreme demon Sakupen Hell with a brighter color palette, a different song, and a boss fight!
Timing extreme in Darwin's classic bright design/effect style. Zoink's easiest level

TMco collab themed around the I Wanna Be The Guy needle games. Mostly black and white with small amounts of rainbow coloration and a heaven theme. The gameplay is very learny and increases in intensity throughout the level.
A classic 2.0 level with challenging, diverse gameplay and icy blue theming. Has an infamous memory part near the end requiring the player to collect 21 keys in a specific order.
Extremely high cps solo level by At424. The spider and wave are very high cps, demanding a lot of stamina.
Originally made as a joke by KrmaL in 2.0 and rated due to a bet with RobTop over the verification, this level is entirely decorated with 1.0 blocks and is extremely imbalanced. What did you expect?

A four and a half minute long, cube only memory level built to be the ultimate endurance test at the time. Features old style decoration and gameplay, and is notable for its insane nerve buildup potential and some harsh chokepoints. The level has 26 distinct sections, one for each mile of the marathon.
A truly hell-themed memory extreme with artistic yet gory designs. Consists of a flashy 2nd drop with heavy usage of teleportals, and an orbless mini cube maze with ship and wave sections in between.
Colorful maymory memory map created by finley and friends.
Faithful Acu spinoff that is almost twice the length of the original. Features many of the same gameplay quirks found in Acu, similar modern deco, and a very hard ending.
Fast, upbeat and fun megacollab started 'way back' in 2019. Took 4 years to complete and another 2 years to get rated.
Fully solo made level by Sdslayer that changes decoration style every couple parts. Gameplay is mostly carried by click-sync but has a few notable chokepoints scattered throughout.

Sequel to "Miscellaneous Memory" by the same creator, being much more polished and well-decorated. The gameplay is incredibly learny yet consistent with a pretty hard last dual. Refer to the creator's tutorial video for easier learning.

The first Extreme Demon made by the legendary creator FunnyGame, themed around the sci-fi series of the same name. The gameplay is often considered to be of poor quality, and the level contains a long cutscene at the beginning.
1.9 style extreme memorable for its incredibly satisfying and well-received gameplay. One of the four levels by Latezk named after Jupiter's four largest moons.
1.9 styled memory level.
A collab between XDjoa and SoggyDash for the Zeronium CC2! Features stinking greyscale effects and fast paced, dual heavy gameplay throughout.

A long invisible level that follows a group of birds through a forest as the days pass by. The gameplay consist of mostly clicksync timings with some high cps parts present at the drops. Features visual indicators such as trigger orbs to guide the player in some parts.
Chaotic rainbow memory extreme using enter & exit effects to the fullest. Contains an intimidating cube maze at 70% with distracting visuals and effects throughout the level.
Bright and colourful circus themed solo extreme that took 2 years to get rated.

Sequel of Techno Flashes that uses the same song. Upgrades the its predecessors decoration by incorporating more complex neon designs and by increasing the energy. The second half features a rainbow color palette and the Flashback Zone™ incase you forgot its a sequel to Techno Flashes.
Unique design extreme created and verified solo, gradually becoming messier and more dreamlike. Contains high-cps gameplay and difficult straight fly sections.

Simple & effective design extreme with a distinct RGBY color scheme. Has many repetitive memory sections that pair well with the song, and also has a highly chaotic QuazeryIceCube style maze at the end with hundreds of possible routes.
A collection of rejected Yatagarasu parts that took 6 years to get rated. It is the second level to feature Terron's bird. The level heavily relies on chokepoints and nerves.

Grayscale with red level, with a lot of blood details. This was initially a nearly-impossible top 1, before being extremely nerfed. While everything's mostly balanced, the wave sections can be quite the difficulty spikes.
An upbeat and colourful extreme set to ANTONYMPH by VyletPony
*Epilepsy Warning*
Old collab level with a lot of familiar faces such as Dorami, Danzmen, and our most popular, Chlorines. Overall its a pretty fun, fast paced level, with a hard predrop.
Solo layout-styled flow level by with a deep blue and black color scheme. Contains difficult duals and timings, and keeps a constant fast pace throughout. Is generally well received.

1.9 styled design level inspired by Toxic Sewers, themed around escaping an underground wastewater facility. Includes lots of subtle effects and movements to build immersion. References the infamous Rupture wave at 40%.

Minimalist solo extreme telling an abstract story about grief. Features creative dual-based gameplay, representing two separate individuals. Garnered controversy for being rated despite its simplicity, though it is extremely well received among victors.

Russian duo level featuring a flashy rainbow color scheme and fast-paced clicksync gameplay. Memorably contains a randomized robot section where you have to collect Super Kontik cookies. "best sandwich cookie you have probably ever seen in your life."

Kivvvi's magnum opus; a well-enjoyed solo extreme 7 months in the making featuring highly detailed designs and artwork with fast-paced clicksync-based flow gameplay. Much of the level's difficulty comes from the first section of the drop, especially in the short wave segments, creating a bit of a stress test for the latter half of the level.
Code themed solo extreme with a predominantly green and red colour scheme, inspired by Toxic Sewers, Rupture, and Controlled Chaos. The drop is mostly comprised of mirrored gameplay.

A 2.0 styled extreme demon with distinct wave sections, tricky ship parts, and diverse click patterns that resembles old styled gameplay, along with appealing yet somewhat simplistic decoration elements.
Very vibrant splitscreen 2 player level with the parts being references to various games. Includes some tricky and fast-paced gameplay, with the beginning being the hardest one.
Solo XXL extreme with a variety of styles, themed around finding forgiveness for mistakes.
Flowy clicksync extreme themed around gambling, featuring a consistent red and black color scheme with many references to cards and casinos.
Solo extreme inspired by the piston from Minecraft! The pistons move the blocks in the level around, making for some interesting moving object heavy gameplay.

Translating to “Orange Blue Pink,” this level uses a strict 3-color palette. The gameplay is unorthodox, with learny duals and memory-based gimmicks. The community seems determined to keep the level at exactly 0 likes on the servers for reasons unknown.
Silly 2.1 memory collab with unorthodox gameplay and structuring and tons of tiny jokes and references. Beware the creature at 21%.
Atmospheric & monochromatic robot-only extreme with a gloomy song by The Neighborhood. Takes subtle inspiration from Zylenox, featuring a fast-paced climax.
Has a very chill atmosphere and gameplay that is mostly timings, wave, and ship. Was supposed to have an extension but was released early.
The third and final level of the Apocalyptic trilogy, featuring very similar gameplay to Cataclysm, but harder.

A pure solo extreme heavily inspired by Eon clocking in at 20 minutes long. Many concepts from Eon are present here, and it takes advantage of its shorter length to experiment more with structures, designs and song representation without inflating its object count. Its gameplay is notable for 3 distinct fast-paced segments starting at 17.2%, 45.8% and 79%, separated by slower, easier gameplay.

2-player duo collab where player 2's part is extreme and player 1's is significantly easier to the point of non-demon gameplay, hence the name. Consists of themeless and pretty low-key visuals, including a review about the mario movie at end. I don't think we're alike at all Mr. White...
Unconventional breakup themed design level with unorthodox orb combinations and psychedelic visuals. Unfortunately the platformer checkpoint at 88% does not let you respawn...

Solo intended 2p level, created for someseal's solo 2p creator contest. The gameplay is high cps, frequently switching between 2p and 1p sections. It's grayscale and effect heavy decoration is based off of both an older unrated level by Jemma, and the Undertale "Disbelief" animation.
A joke cat themed remake of both Aquamarine and Planet Circles. Features a long and easy predrop followed by an extremely hard wave. Has an SC66P inspired part and the PG Clubstep cat.
A fast paced megacollab co-hosted by MrFreckles and Rynoxious that has been in development since 2021!

1.6 Extreme demon megacollab that features vibrant colours, several tricky ship sections and a difficult predrop. The gameplay still manages to feel modern and polished despite its limitations. Generally considered to be the most well received 1.6 extreme.
An old 2.0 pseudo-memory level featuring unique designs and moving objects, very hard ball timings, and lots of text portals. LDM ball cube ball big cube ball next...

We are experiencing technical difficulties displaying this level's video, due to Sony Music Entertainment blocking it. Please replace or mute the song in your record if you plan on beating this level, as we can't look at your record if we can't see the video.
Memory level known for being goofy and having a funny bossfight. Is skewed towards mainly ship gameplay.

Generally well-received timing and memory-based extreme demon with a green and red corrupted technological decoration that was made in 2.1. It was inspired by the 1.9 insane demon Chaotic Machine and is similar to Killbot although it contains less flashes. Has a very difficult ending.
FRANK
The sequel to Lost Love that will really test your ability to memorize a path and ability to learn duals.
Originally created in 2.0 and got a bugfix and decoration update in 2.1. It had one of the earliest uses of the dual wave gimmick where both waves share the same gravity.
Well-received dual-based megacollab featuring a consistent green and yellow palette and great gameplay. Memorable for its flashy effects and learny duals

A peaceful but extremely hard to learn memory level. Features a part where you must break every block in order to progress which does not work in practice mode. Also features a terrifying vertical memory wave at the end.
Wulzy’s first created extreme taking a twenty-seven video long playlist and 678 days from start to finish. Features several parts with different effects and skillsets. Overall very well received.
A collage style fast paced level that switches style with each part. The difficulty is ending carried, and the level features many bursts of high cps gameplay.

Design style memory level using control: mind, and is somewhat reminiscent of Sleepless by ChaSe gameplay wise. Features some split path gameplay and a cube maze around the halfway point. Sadly has nothing to do with actual brainrot so do not expect to find Triple T or 67 kid.
Themed off of the Mario Kart Wii track by the same name, this gold mine themed level has many references to its source material, and is also generally very well received.

A unique extreme demon featuring many double-clicks. The gameplay is learny and somewhat inconsistent but satisfying, reflected by its mixed reception. Most of the difficulty is condensed into the cubes at the beginning and 71%, which include fixed hitboxes.
ItsMeGeoGD's latest modern extreme! Features sync gameplay and some very fabulous wave gaps.
An iconic 2.0 extreme featuring blood-red theming and unconventional gameplay, with infamous sections such as the 47% wave spam and the ending cube.
A faithful remake of Marathon, rebalanced to remove chokepoints and emphasize nerve buildup and consistency. The decoration gets gradually more complex as the level progresses
Peaceful woodland themed solo extreme featuring slow paced gameplay and an asymmetrical dual.
A 2-player memory level by akunakun that was made in one sitting, with mostly path-based memory other than the splitscreen dual.
Short extreme that switches styles halfway through, with one of the biggest wave chokepoints in its difficulty range.
BLBL inspired extreme demon originally made 4 years ago, now fully updated and reverified by DaMeister.
A 2-player level that splits apart and then recombines together in the end. Visuals contain a lot of contrasting effects and feature rainbow and monochrome palette.

An extreme that's alike to Nhelv, even down to the song. The theming is of a struggle with mental health which is represented through its well-created, surreal effects in the decoration and its predominently black, white and red coloring which becomes very colorful nearing the end. Also features well-received, unorthodox gameplay with several dual sections, especially 83% - 86% due to the horizontally uneven ship gameplay.

A modern extreme themed around biomechanics and the circulatory system. It features artwork in both the background and the foreground, fusing the two themes. Mainly features D-block wave gameplay and vertical dash orbs throughout the level, and explores unconventional gameplay ideas for its runtime with the intention of encapsulating the energy of the song.
Buffed Acu remake featuring a very similar click pattern and glow deco. Has an AI generated name.
A chair designed for efficiency and comfort. (Purple and yellow extreme mainly featuring ship and wave gameplay, but also features a swing dual and a multi-creator triple trial at the end.)

A very long solo art level inspired by many other XL art levels such as Emerald Realm and Well Rested. The gameplay gets progressively faster paced and intense towards the end, and it features a lot of spider/spider orb gameplay. One of the most enjoyed extremes.
Twan's first solo!!!
Hideki's two player level finally rated year's after its release

Memory extreme with QuazeryIceCube's signature freeform gameplay with many possible routes, and simple but effective decoration. The first half contains most of the difficulty, and a handful of timing chokepoints.
An easy extreme demon megacollab hosted by Vortrox to celebrate the success of his “GD news” video series on Youtube. It contains unique well-rounded flow gameplay.
A fast-paced extreme collab filled with brutal gameplay complemented with glow-style decoration. Notoriously has a very chokable last wave and ship.
Ruins themed level with calm deco and gameplay, mainly based in slow timings of cube and robot, it has surprisingly hard parts for its placement due to the duration of the level.
An early 2.1 XXL megacollab hosted by Quiken, infamous for having unbalanced gameplay and the 47% orange orb timing.
A solo extreme by Cordeaux dedicated to fellow creator Onvil for their birthday!
High energy memory megacollab verified by LordVadercraft with flashy effects and dense, rainbow filled decoration. Has a notoriously difficult last click.
A four minute long 1.9GDPS megacollab featuring parts made by GrenadeofTacos' family members. Has mostly fast paced, learny and well rounded gameplay. Also has a Toyota
Waterbound's second extreme demon, this time created in a minimal but atmospheric design in 24 hours. Uses only the cube gamemode once again.
Dark red castle themed Cherryteam collab, verified and published by Denni

Remake of Thinking Space II, rated as a low end extreme demon. It was created as a solo level by KZLR at the request of his friend Neeple, who wanted to verify an extreme demon level. Features fast paced cube and ship gameplay with an infamously difficult last jump.
An easier but similarly fast paced clicksync sequel to ATMarbl. Features a hard last spider and Temp's insane wave part.

A faithful remake of Eiken's famous 1.9 insane demon The Four Elements. Took over a year to create, and each part features detailed and well themed decoration using 1.9 limitations. The gameplay is similar to the original but much harder.
Modern solo extreme with a long and complex asymmetrical dual in the second half.
BOIII WHAT U SAY ABOUT PHONK??

Extremely colourful and upbeat XL megacollab made by a friend group. Features learny 2.2 feature heavy gameplay, with some unorthodox flow at the drop. The decoration and gameplay are highly varied between parts, creating a very diverse playing experience. "Imagine a place where people of all walks of life can come together and bro down."

A slow-paced, progression-oriented solo memory extreme, with the gameplay being based on the same repeating structure cycling through the different orb types with each iteration and the path forward being almost invisible, taking many unexpected twists and turns. The visuals and structuring get more complex as the level progresses, though it stays simple with its limited use of gamemodes and being entirely slow-speed.
A modern mashup style level with 2.2 camera effects featuring a French dessert. The gameplay is mainly made up of click sync based timings with notably hard wave chokepoints.

Old impossible level inspired extreme featuring difficult, learny gameplay restricted to update 1.2. Received a significant nerfdate moving it down 300 spots in mid-2024. Contains lighthearted rainbow decoration while using the entirety of Dry Out.
Colorful clicksync extreme themed around the symbol "four" in Japanese, having a similar pronunciation as the symbol "death." Known for having hard wave sections and fast-paced timings.

A 1.9 GDPS solo extreme heavily comprised of learny sync gameplay and some quite difficult wave timings. There is a notable skip that can be performed at 76%. Also known for being one of the hardest levels to place on the IDL when it was a misrated insane demon, though it never made it to the top 1 spot due to Time Pulse also being insane demon at the time.
Level with a very unique and (ironically) dreamy style, sharing its name with the used song by Against All Logic. Features gameplay mainly focused on cube timings and ship.
Pretty level which is extremely front loaded, with the predrop carrying a good portion of the difficulty. Focuses on timings.
Short and atmospheric extreme named after a river in New Zealand, and has a unusual tech-savanna-with-black-hole theme. The gameplay is mostly ship and wave focused. Hawk

Flowy & clean design collab using a not-so-garbage rock song by the band Garbage. Memorable for its dynamic effects and movements paired with engaging and well-received gameplay. Also features fantastic color work! Verified by Zeronium.
Megacollab remake of Paladin by Asonicmen, and references Dragon Quest. Has faithful mid 2.1 design style decoration, and well rounded gameplay.
Graphic design style collab and sequel to Unfair Evening. Notable for being extremely short at only 35 seconds long, and features a tough randomised angled wave spam at the end.

Former hack verified top 1 by Ozpectro, later reverified legitimately by SkyJax after being unrated. Overall plays like a high end insane demon except for the iconic, extremely hard wave around 50%. Also has a gimmicky dual ship which some find awkward, and a handful of bugs to avoid. We love Fexty!
The first Russian extreme demon megacollab. It doesn't have a consistent theme in either gameplay or decoration, aside from the general 2.0 aesthetic.
Highly skill based extreme with fast paced flow gameplay with an emphasis on wave. Smoking kills.
A 2-player level, a part of the gang trilogy. The level's name is meant to be a British version of Based Gang. Has a key you can collect to turn the bossfight icons into the Bass Cave demon.

Mechanical solo extreme highlighting DreamZone's classic dense and industrial design style. Features constant effects and movements, creating an incredibly dynamic atmosphere with fast-paced gameplay and well-received dual sections.

A 1.9 megacollab hosted by Andromeda, containing many different iconic creators like Cyclic and ViPriN. Originally hack-verified, it would be one of the few extreme demons created and verified in 1.9. Generally poorly received due to the inconsistent duals, awkward spam and poor balancing.
Nine Circles level which is inspired by Falling up and Black Blizzard. Legend has it, a mod played this level for 6% in practice mode, watched the showcase and didn’t send it because of the gameplay.
markus

You wouldn't believe it, but this level's an extreme memory mix. Interestingly, it remixes beginner to main list memory extremes while maintaining engaging and well-received gameplay & balancing. Notably chooses nicher memory extremes than other levels to "be cooler," such as Santa Fe, GO bird and Hollow.
Collab hosted by Metalface221. Very unique sync-based level with bright effect decoration and one of the longest straight-flies of any rated extreme demon.

A level built by Manix648 for KrmaL in response to an offhand joke made by RobTop, featuring completely invisible gameplay. In comparison to the visible version that came later, some aspects of the gameplay are much more difficult and unpredictable.
A Zoink Doink collab that was in the works for more than 3 years, featuring extremely learny clicksync gameplay, with the first half being especially difficult.
A minimalistic style level that is reflected both in the deco and the fact the level only uses the cube gamemode. Features a long intro cutscene and some punishing custom hitboxes.

Solo-intended 2p level created and verified by Pocke. Uses a lot of gimmicks where the second player input does things like changing the player's size or the colour of an orb. Generally a good start for getting into solo 2p.

A remake of Hi by KrmaL. The level was poorly received, and the creator asked for it to be deleted off the servers but was denied by moderators. As it's a buffed version of the original, the gameplay is gimmicky, chokepoint heavy, and has a very hard second half.
Solo extreme with light gradient decoration reminiscent of Rust. Has mainly timing based gameplay, and a ship at the end with a lot of orbs.
High quality level themed around a computer breaking down. Features mainly sync based gameplay, some hard waves, and a mirrored section at the end.
Easy extreme demon most notable for the extremely hard wave in the mid points. The rest of the level is considerably easier except for a few hard ship gaps.

Influential red flow megacollab, inspiring many other levels and essentially acting as a blueprint for modern flow gameplay. Features quintessential flow gameplay: learny, fast paced, high cps, clicksync based gameplay with frequent gamemode switches and some tough short waves.
Solo level by DrCuber. As the name implies, this level is purely cube gameplay with various timing gimmicks. Has a notoriously hard first part, and two parts with an orb that follows the player.

Solo extreme with heavy rainbow decoration and a generally silly and playful theme. Features mostly timing based gameplay, with an emphasis on cube and robot. Was somehow insane demon for a week, causing it to place on the Insane Demon List as one of the hardest top 1s in its history. It was then promoted to extreme an hour later :trollface:
Originally an unfinished level named Tazz by Shocksidian, finished up and published by AAAAAlex
Has an overall horrible reputation, due to the beginning, and the infamous last third, having the 90% click of all time.

Spanish megacollab hosted by Youtuber & streamer LastPrismAlex. Notably received an update almost 4 years later, halving the objects and generally improving the decoration while adding 2.2 effects. Features a consistent rainbow color scheme and designs still reminiscent of the original version verified in 2021.

A slow and very atmospheric XL extreme using an equally atmospheric song to match. Features detailed block designs and some memory sections. Gets generally harder as the level progresses, ending with a short, slow, but very narrow nine circles style wave.

The prequel to STARCRASH with gameplay made by SoggyCat and decorated by ClingingBog. Set in an abandoned city, where a star creation experiment is left unmaintained. The player must reach the top of the factory to stop this experiment, or the star will collapse. Notable for its high-CPS clicksync dual gameplay throughout the drop.
One of the first dual heavy extreme demons to exist. Overall pretty fun and very learny, especially the cube at 65%.

Flamboyant My Hero Academia themed megacollab finished in 2019 hosted by ILRELL mixing art, modern, and design, in which every part is based off a quirk of a student. Memorable for its somewhat charming lack of cohesion and impressive roster of iconic early 2.1 creators. Gameplay is surprisingly high-quality and intuitive for its age.
A long and dark clicksync-based level, themed after trains in both it's deco and song. The gameplay is learny and heavy on timings, with some hard cube and ship gameplay.
A solo extreme that took 1 year to make. Has distinct parts in its art decoration and its timing-based gameplay leading up to the player's ascension at the end.
Harder version of Red World, with most its difficulty being ship and swing copter gameplay.
Enfur's first 2.2 level which uses a rainbow theme and is much more accessible than their other levels. YIPPEE!!!
Russian for 'Addiction,' this level features unusual cube only gameplay and extremely bright and unsettling story-based decoration.

A tribute to all sonic series levels hosted by MinAY! The gameplay, decoration, and song choice are all inspired by the old sonic series levels, with a particular emphasis on HyperSonic's early 2.1 style.
1.9 Christmas-themed megacollab hosted by Youknowwho.
Jenkins level with very unique decoration at the time, and very unique yet awkward gameplay.
Arraegen's entry in the Zeronium CC2 Creator Contest! Uses player colors for the colors of the decoration.
Cute love-themed level with amazing decoration and click-sync, flow based gameplay. Some transitions can be an issue for some.
Deceptively simple beginning until the difficulty spikes in the second half. Nerve wracking as a result.
Iconic for its challenging wave in the beginning, and very precise ship.
A remake of Sky Tech, containing updated decoration that is also quite colorful. This remake retains a similar gameplay style, though it buffs the wave segments of Sky Tech by quite a bit.
Remake of the old impossible level Elite Z. Primarily known for the infamous two-player straight fly and the "So Pro?" UFO spam.
Short level that's fairly chokepoints heavy, most notably Jenkins' extremely fast part.
A level inspired by volume and made as an attribute to Metalface. Boost a couple similarities to Volume, most notably having a pretty difficult wave section in the middle of the level.
Strange, poorly received modern extreme from 2020 that has been described as a superbuffed 4 star.
A remake of Alphabet X by a group of Polish creators. Known for a double blue orb timing that appears in the level multiple times.
Red glow layout style clicksync level, based on phonk memes and as such featuring a lot of trollfaces. Very tightly synced, and known for it's hard duals.
The first Legendary rated extreme demon. An energetic, high quality megacollab with a signature green style. Gameplay is fast paced and engaging, and so learny at times that it borders on memory.

A 28 person megacollab made as the last level ever made by Rlol. The decoration is colorful and reminiscent of party lights. The gameplay and song reflect this, being fast-paced and energetic. Has a notable lack of cohesion between parts creating a chaotic but light hearted, fun atmosphere

A very large megacollab featuring many Finnish and Korean creators. The decoration and gameplay vary a lot throughout the three minute runtime, but much of the difficulty is condensed into a few chokepoints.
Surprisingly high quality joke remake of Ultrasonic, featuring an extension consisting of multiple other sonic series inspired parts. Every part in the level is made by Sans Undertale.
The hardest level in the An Gyung trilogy. It is mostly fast-paced with a slower predrop. The beginning is considered the hardest part, containing many awkward chokepoints.

Cavern themed art megacollab featuring timing based gameplay in the first half of the level and fast paced click sync based gameplay in the second half. Used to be harder than Eternal Moment, but received a major nerfdate when it fell out of the top 150.

An effect layout masterpiece spanning over 7 minutes long. The gameplay is mostly comprised of learny clicksync, which intensifies as the level progresses. The level is themed around an unsolved internet ARG, Cicada 3301, with many easter eggs and QR codes scattered throughout the level referencing the puzzles. Received a bugfix update which made it become one of the most enjoyed extremes in the game.
Bizaare's ode to the simpler side of Geometry Dash. An xl memory level using deliberately simple designs and subtle effects, and prioritising song representation above all else.
Colorful dark level and the second level of the Dedication Series, with most of its difficulty in the middle parts.
A first-half heavy sequel that's based off of a comedy-horror film of the same name. Features a variety of different fast-paced gameplay types, including a bossfight at 70%.

Most notable for its random offset gimmick, where the gameplay is offset from the visible decoration. Most of the difficulty comes from the gimmick, making this one of the most unique easy extremes. Due to the nature of the gimmick and how much easier this level is when fully visible, liveplay is required when submitting.

Solo extreme with over 200 hours of editor work where you break out of prison and traverse through forests and cityscapes as you attempt to escape the police. Its gameplay is full of gamemode switches and has a few camera gimmicks, and the deco has many easter eggs.
"sorry for gameplay lol"
Well known megacollab.  Consists of overall awkward gameplay, but can also be pretty fun.
Was formerly way harder and poorly received, after the update its just poorly received now.
A four and a half minute long level, going through the countries of the world. Made and verified solo, on an ipad

A nine minute long extreme with simple but very effective yellow decoration and great song representation. Contains mostly slow paced and easy gameplay, but has some difficult dual parts, a hard last wave, and lots of fixed hitboxes. A true test of endurance and nerve control.

Solo-intended 2p extreme, solo created by ranoutofusers. The deco is extremely bright and colourful, with the gameplay being 2nd half carried. This was users' first rate after getting 95 sends in total.
The second half is a bit harder than the first

Levels.Nombre: V O L L E Y

Levels.Descripcion: A red effect solo extreme with an unsettling atmosphere. Contains a short memory section in the second half.

An older Loltad layout decorated in 2.2 by Loltad and IceRod. Features complex memory gameplay and uses the second half of Theory of Everything 2. Perhaps most notable for receiving an incredible twelve 100s in a row on EDEL. One of the most enjoyed extremes.
Very raw Jeyzor level with extremely hard duals and a funny bossfight at the end.
Megacollab featuring a variety of skillsets, but has a major difficulty spike in the final wave and ship. Has some long UFO gravity portal worms and a rather goofy song.

A beginner extreme with fast-paced flowy and learny gameplay by TeamUprising that uses a mix of all gamemodes. The difficulty of the gameplay increases near the end. Its glow-style decoration is prominently pink, purple and blue in its coloring and has a technological theming. Has a high object count of 256k.
Very similar to polish alphabet, but more fun and learny duals.

Beginner extreme Sonic Wave remake built by Zest as redemption for hacking Sonic Wave three years prior. Features significantly altered gameplay compared to the other remakes, including ship and UFO sections at the drop in reference to the original pre-update Sonic Wave. Generally the most well received extreme sonic wave remake.
Very old hell level that predates Yatagarasu, with precise timings and some fast ship parts. May not quite live up to its name.

Very pink level built as the creator's first finished deco project, a level where you must party without being caught by the eyeball police. Contains many different kinds of gameplay and is generally well received.

A fast paced level with multiple insane chokepoints, most notably the 4% 240hz frame perfect, the 69% blind click, and the wave gaps at 63% and 74%. Was somehow formerly rated Insane Demon, and became an insider meme on the Insane Demon List.

Bright rainbow design extreme known for its iconic hyperpop song and easily recognizable party-like visuals by StarkyTheSalad. The gameplay is well-received, consisting of learny & well-synced cube sections and clever fakes.

An electric and futuristic city-themed collaboration with distinct parts, bright colors and a mixture of detailed designs and effects. The gameplay is regarded as being rather learny thanks to the complex dual gameplay. There are also chokepoints throughout, notably the dual ship at the 60% mark.

A “demon mix” type of level with around 40 seconds of gameplay with a lot of popular extremes, such as Acheron, Firework and Bloodbath with clean but simple decoration made in 2.1 by the content creator Vit12. The level contains several chokepoints and is first-half carried. It’s also the prequel to The Ultimate Return.

Darwin solo extreme from mid 2.1 reminiscent of Rupture, ToE2 and Blast Processing. Most well known for its absurd ship chokepoint at the drop, and the rest of the level plays more like an insane demon.
A solo extreme using only spikes for decoration! Features unusual gameplay, including a diagonal asymmetrical ship.
Flashy pink & blue megacollab featuring incredibly learny and frantic gameplay and a nebulous space theme. Notably difficult to learn for an easy extreme but satisfying to complete.
2.0 level which has chokepoints and bugs scattered through out, the most iconic of which is the extremely hard wave with a random UFO break in the middle of it.

1.9 styled Flamewall inspired extreme, now in violet! Uses the final two minutes of the song, and features near non-stop fast paced gameplay, with a difficulty increase in the second half. Activating the LDM makes the decoration pure 1.9, while the full detail version has some 2.2 features. Enable shake at own risk...

A predominantly skill-based beginner extreme which was worked on for 8 months. Features colourful design decoration and a very upbeat song by Waterflame. Has all-around gameplay with the hardest part generally being considered the dual section from 58% to 70%.

An upbeat solo extreme taking inspiration from numerous design creators and featuring the popular pop song of the same name. Has some learny and unusual but well synced gameplay and a very complex dual at the end.
Short and fairly learny level that was placed at #3 on IDL when it got rated. Features a fast paced rainbow first half and a monochrome ending with some tricky timings.
A very old 2.0 level with poorly aged decoration but better gameplay. Has a complex asymmetrical dual in the first half. One of the oldest sync focused extremes.
Very purple and green, and the gameplay consists of fast paced click sync, which can be pretty fun. Somehow its XL even though it doesnt feel that long.

A solo level originally made for the GDS Creator Contest, though it missed the submission deadline. As a remake of and sequel to Dark Travel, it has a similar structure while significantly improving on decoration in each section.

A solo extreme demon that has very bizarre, unconventional yet intriguing art decoration attached with a heavy amount of variety. The gameplay matches this decoration style by being heavily unorthodox.

A massive community project started by Spu7Nix, inspired by r/place. Built by over 14,000 players, this is one of the largest Geometry Dash collabs to ever be made, with countless ways to get through the level.

The first part of the Ocular Miracle Trilogy, featuring stunning decoration for the time and fast paced gameplay. Has some janky sections in the mid parts and most notably entirely lacks a drop. A former misrated insane demon until 2024, it reigned as a formidable IDL top 5, including time at top 1, for many years before being finally promoted.
A harder remake of 8o, keeping the same formatting as the original level. The decoration features more glow and effects, while keeping the same simplistic block design.
Solo extreme by lazer that repeats sections of a small amount of gameplay, unlocking more sections when the time signature in the song changes. Difficulty spikes at the 60% wave.

A 1.6 styled level started in early 2.1 and finished in 2.2. Known for being one of the best ship based beginner extremes. Has an asymmetrical dual in the middle and a hard Electrodynamix / 8o style ending ship.
Solo extreme by Kreno set to the Gorillaz song of the same name. Has a fully greyscale colour scheme and skill based gameplay.

An extreme demon with a light-hearted frosty theming, having vibrant and varied shades of blue as well as a mixture of effect and design decoration. The gameplay is fast-paced and features all-around learny gameplay.
Extremely short extreme primarily inspired by Deadlocked. Known for having tough ship chokepoints and a brutal last wave, and also allows you to take multiple swag routes for increased aura points.
A high quality megacollab by the BloomOcean team themed around the solar eclipse and the mythology surrounding it.
Sillow extreme demon which, like their others, consists of mostly skill based gameplay, mostly wave and ship.
An XL Hexagon Force remake using the second half of the song. Features a long asymmetrical dual in the second half with lots of swingcopter gameplay using unusual gamemodes.
A 5 minute XL level created for the #levelution movement during 2.1. The gameplay is mostly comprised of timings and clicksync with a sharp difficulty spike in the middle of the level.

A skill based flow level with an outdoor theme featuring many asymmetrical duals and hard waves. Features some challenging wave chokepoints in the first half, difficult duals throughout, and ends with a challenging click consistency dual wave. Also features an Undertale remix, meaning you may have a bad time...

A unique minimalistic memory level using simple but effective block structures on a dark background. The gameplay is very freeform, and the large maze at the end has an immeasurable number of possible routes.

A very quirky timings focused level with many gimmicks. Has many fake spikes in the beginning spider and the brutal ending ball. Only has two ships, with one being very orb focused, and the other skill focused. Is very second half heavy with the second ship and the ball carrying most of the difficulty.

6 minute solo memory extreme using the entirety of the eponymous Sweet Trip song, and featuring high quality early 2000s WindowsXP style deco inspired by the album cover. Has mostly 2.2 physics memory ship gameplay through its runtime, and has an unusual alternating blind clicksync wave as well as other gimmicks. Made memory through it's confusing, constantly moving, and highly obscured gameplay (Including hiding your icon behind jumpingcat3.png).

whlt's first solo extreme. It's extremely short at only 40 seconds long, and has pastel-colored effect decoration. The gameplay syncs well with the song and consists of 4 parts, with the gimmick of each part being increasingly difficult as the level goes on.

The long standing top 1 on the Insane Demon List before getting promoted. A 1.9 memory level built to showcase the update's capabilities instead of trying to look like a 1.9 level. Has two endings, though the 'good ending' requires a tough frame perfect timing far into the level.
One of the most well known extreme demons. The first level in the Apocalyptic trilogy. Consists of a lot of difficult ship parts and an extremely hard beginning wave.
May or may not be MrPoopyBurger's worst level...

Bright and effect-based memory extreme demon loosely themed around heartbreak. Consists of very well-received memory gameplay and hazy, atmospheric backgrounds. Definitely a fantastic introduction to memory extremes!

Dark and emotional XXL+ solo level with minimalistic but effective decoration. Nearly entirely greyscale, but gains a small but meaningful amount of colour at the second drop. The gameplay is heavily endurance based, and has multiple split paths and frequent timings. Took 4 years to get featured.
Exscher's first serious attempt at getting a rated level. An insanely detailed art level with some small two player segments.

An extreme with a theming around the streaming platform which is featured in its pre-drop and ending; it otherwise features purple-colored glow decoration. Contains flowy and learny gameplay with the wave parts being most prevalent in difficulty.

An extreme that was formerly #1 on the Insane Demon list. Originally made in 2.0, though was reworked in 2.1. Features a mostly red and orange color scheme with its simpler decoration style. The gameplay is all-around with its gamemodes, though the wave parts can prove quite a challenge.

A beginner 1.9PS extreme demon megacollab. Manages to capture the essence of old megacollabs such as Supersonic with its varied decoration styles. Has an all-around fast-paced gameplay style with difficult ship and old swingcopter sections. Each part was built only after the previous part had been completed.
Beginner extreme megacollab featuring multiple steamhappy cameos and a very silly tone overall.
Short timing level focused on clicking exactly to the songs beat, Typically well received due to being very satisfying.
Predominantly greyscale modern level with a Kasane Teto song! Contains some confusing memory parts and a few camera flips.

An extreme demon by the large creation team SpinStudios, which gives it a very varying glow decoration style emphasising effects and design with a mostly red and orange color scheme. Contains flowy and fast paced gameplay with difficult wave sections.
Formerly a normal early 2.1 Extreme Demon, but due to some updates the level has pretty much become the equivalent to a griefed Minecraft server. Video showcase is of the latest version.

Very bright and intense space rainbow level in Vit12's signature style. Also contains Vit's signature simple, skillbased gameplay style which can be divisive, though this time with better transitions and playtesting.

Complex & intuitive memory extreme with unconventional, flowy gameplay. Features unique gameplay tropes like breakable blocks and a ship section controlled by a green orb. Gameplay is extremely well-received.

A passion project megacollab hosted by Loc9e over 6 years in the making! Features Woogi inspired decoration with tasteful usage of glow, and a Porter Robinson song mashup. The gameplay is very well received and features learny/memory sections and a handful of duals. The 85% pink orb is not as hard as it used to be.
Extreme demon with a consistent glow decoration style that shifts colors throughout. Has timings-based gameplay with there being a difficulty spike at the ending.

A skill-based Extreme Demon comprised of heavy wave and ship gameplay, as well as some fake orbs and somewhat difficult timings. Notably a very popular beginner Extreme, due to the gameplay being relatively straightforward and easy to learn.

Unorthodox extreme with a slow pre-drop which heightens in both pace and difficulty at the drop with the waves being the hardest parts. The effects are very flashy and aim to obscure the player's vision.
A short and intense UFO-only extreme. Has distinct segments with differing styles of effect decoration. Contains very unorthodox and learny gameplay, including 2P and a boss fight section.
The last extreme demon from 2.0. Each section is styled after one of Pennutoh's other levels, and as such they vary a lot. Its gameplay is learny and fast-paced, and has all-round balancing.
A solo extreme themed around the game Outer Wilds. The gameplay is gimmicky with some hard timings and varying gravity, and there's a minigame section based on the game before the drop.

A remake to ZenthicAlpha's hard demon, Crimson Chamber. Heavily revamps the gameplay with 2.2 mechanics, and updates the decoration while staying true to the original. The gameplay balancing is all-around with some difficult dual sections.
A design deco factory-themed extreme demon, with many different unique gimmicks throughout. The difficulty is heavily carried by the wave section at 66%, and it's overall very learny.
Almost two minutes of pure silent clubstep cube maze. Be very afraid...

A city themed level with unusual dreamy landscapes and whimsical nature. Very chill but nerve racking gameplay with a vertical part and a fully randomised part in the middle of the level. Enjoy the walk before those beautiful cities get destroyed in the disaster!

A red and gray-colored beginner megacollab extreme that captures the style of old 2.0 levels with both its decoration being influenced by Artificial Ideology, and its unconventional gameplay style. The gameplay itself is all-around, though the wave parts are slightly more difficult.

A well-received slow-paced extreme demon with vibrant colors with eye-catching, glitchy effects, and a route around the start that changes the colour scheme. The gameplay is precision-based timings built with no spikes, which can take getting used to but do get consistent.
A megacollab hosted by DanZmeN and verified by Golden, featuring tricky, fast-paced timings, difficult wave sections and overall janky gameplay. Has an infamous mini-wave at the end of the level.
A Zeronium solo level themed around FUN FRIDAY! Where many fun things can happen, on a Friday. Contains multiple references to fun and silly things from Zeronium's streams.
Four minute wave only extreme that gets faster and more intense as the level progresses. Despite being an all wave level, the majority of the difficulty comes from consistency and nerve control.

An extreme similar to Reverence, with flowy gameplay and red and blue effecty glow decoration. The gameplay is learny and carried by the wave segments, with several bugs and chokepoints throughout the level.
Extremely long and well received level with pixel decoration and an intense song. Features mostly clicksync based gameplay, and has a hard dual in the second half.
Medium length megacollab that is surprisingly 1.9 themed. Has an ancient level ID that was updated.

A reta-styled extreme which takes much aspects in decoration and gameplay from the levels it is styled upon. The gameplay is typical of a level of its style: highly flowy and features a lot of clicksync. A lot of the difficulty is condensed into the middle sections. Took a couple of years for it to get rated.
Well known atmospheric XL level with generally slow low cps timing based gameplay and a dual at the end. Has a long cutscene at the start.

Freedom08 remake built entirely in the 1.6 editor. Showcases a variety of deco and gameplay styles throughout its 4 minute length, however sacrifices some of its intensity as the entire level is in 1x speed.
Very well known easy reta style extreme with the typical fast paced flow gameplay, purple glow decoration, and Yoasobi song. One of the most popular beginner extremes.

Extremely high-quality extreme demon that is very well-received. Contains intense and overall complex gameplay which makes it learny, especially the dual segments. Also features a gimmick nearing the end where eight heart shards must be collected in order to complete the level.

Electricity themed solo with simple design and effects, and a mixture of clicksync and timing based gameplay. Despite receiving a large nerf, it is highly unbalanced. Most of the difficulty comes from the middle sections and the very hard wave near the end. (verification video was privated/deleted)
A fast-paced, learny megacollab. The level is praised for its decoration, having detailed designs and effects, enhanced by the extremely vivid rainbow color scheme.

An extreme demon focused on ship, timings and swingcopter gameplay that is highly received, with a satisfying flow. The art decoration has a theming of a submerged and overgrown city that the player falls into after the first third.

Long and cute rainbow coloured extreme with an equally playful song. Mostly timing based, especially in the spider sections, but also features a hard dual and a challenge-like first wave. Has multiple double clicks.

A very well-received extreme demon. The fast-paced, all-around gameplay of the level is highly learny and requires high CPS. The decoration is colorful, and it focuses on vibrant designs and effects which add to the intensity of the level.

An extreme demon which has a very well-regarded theming of a desolate and decaying urban world captured through its purely greyscale coloring, design and art decoration style and the very fitting song-choice. The gameplay has been criticised for feeling tedious.

Sequel to the insane demon Corrosion. The decoration is of a similar style to its predecessor, altered to reflect the heightened intensity of the song. Builds off of Corrosion's gameplay through an increase in difficult timings, a faster pace and higher complexity through the use of 2.2 mechanics.

The final level in the For Matilda series. Features a mixture of design and art decoration which makes every segment distinct. The gameplay is timings-based and has an unconventional style. The final part of the level is a precise minigame section where multiple cubes have differing zooms and angles.
2.0 level based on the infamous hack verified ozpectro levels, it has been subject to a multitude of buffs over the years, and is now known for awkward gameplay and two absurd predrop triple spikes.

A sequel to insane demon Lin Anya. Features mostly all-around learny gameplay, though the ship is more prominent than the other gamemodes. The level mixes design, art and effect decoration with its vibrant and colorful glow style.
Dorami hosted megacollab featuring parts inspired by old popular levels, in a similar style to Idols. Known for having very challenging dual chokepoints.

An extreme demon collaboration between Xaro and WOOGI1411 from all the way back in 2.0 that took several years to get rated. Contains colorful decoration that is standard of the time. The gameplay is all-around and learny, with several chokepoints. My Eye :(

The first 2-player extreme in Geometry Dash. Was verified by four different people swapping positions mid-completion. The decoration is in DanZmeN's typicial 2019 style. Features learny segments and a bossfight with arrows that are not entirely accurate.
A 2-player level that takes inspiration from Bang Gang. In order to make it more feasible to do solo, as the final 20% can be nerfed in exchange for not getting the coin.

A beginner extreme demon worked on for several years with its decoration focusing on a colorful glow design style with a mixture of some effects. The flowy gameplay has a mixture of pacing with the first 33% generally being considered the hardest section.

2019 design-style extreme demon megacollab that lacks a coherent theme. The gameplay is all-around and fast-paced. The ending segment can be a significant chokepoint, as the wave and ship in it are more challenging than the previous segments.

Very short, looksmaxxing-themed beginner extreme, barely over half a minute long. Inspired by Cobwebs and Future Chaos, it features fast-paced flow gameplay with some tough ship and wave parts and high-quality design deco. Has quickly become one of the most popular extremes in the game despite still being very new.

A well-received medium-length extreme which contains a mixture of memory gameplay and timings throughout. The decoration emphasises design and is prominently blue with its coloring. Features a very memorable transition at the 71% mark. Has no wave and very minimal ship, making this a very accessible first extreme to low refresh rate users.

One of the more popular beginner extremes. Very light-hearted and unconventional in its structuring and colorful decoration style. The gameplay mixes memory gameplay with some precise timings. It also gives the player the freedom of having multiple paths to choose from, especially after the pre-drop.
A 1.9-style solo extreme with various styles of decoration throughout. Has generally skill-based ship and timings gameplay, with a difficult dual part at the drop.

A solo extreme that's the sequel to the medium demon 'nguyen bang qua'. Very experimental with its decoration with intense flashes and colors. The timing-heavy gameplay starts off with a slower-pace which quickens in its learny second-half.

A solo extreme by smarted, themed as a lost pilot animation made in the analog VHS era, inspired by the Jumping Devils song animation. The deco has a lot of custom lineart and effects. The gameplay consists of sync-based duals, and changes direction a lot throughout the level.

A 2-player level that has no consistent theme, as there is "no sense of continuity in dreams". For 2-player play it is borderline extreme demon gameplay, and has been rated as insane demon in the past.

A short and extremely silly rainbow level inspired by The Wiener. Features a hard first cube, clicksync gameplay, heavy shader and camera-trigger use, an incomprehensible spam dual, and, of course, the super hotdog itself. The high CPS/spammy nature of this level's gameplay can make this level difficult to approach if you are beating this as one of your first extreme demons.

The sequel to the insane demon DESTROYED which expands on its dual gameplay with a longer level length and has an overall higher CPS. Its high-quality design decoration features a very similar theme to its predecessor where you flee a burning facility that's being destroyed.

An extended remake of the 30 second long "Segmentation Fault." A highly unique extreme using only the cube gamemode but in unusual and gimmicky ways. This includes a maximum click section and many parts where an orb is taped to your cube. The strange gameplay is accompanied by appropriately unusual effects.

A solo remake of the unrated hard demon "Unfound Emotions" with near-identical base gameplay. Its decoration style is similar, but it also introduces tasteful colour usage, especially in the drop to contrast it from the more grayscale predrop and ending. Despite its difficulty often being debated over extreme or insane demon, its ship parts are especially challenging for its difficulty.
squeak (cute clicksync level featuring mostly cube and spider gameplay)

The most popular first extreme, for a good reason. Overall extremely well received for its accessible and fun gameplay throughout. Notably very 60hz friendly, and most of the difficulty is near the start and end.

A 3 minute long pure solo extreme using a pixelation effect where each pixel is visibly split into its RGB subpixels, much like how actual monitor screens work. Its base gameplay is relatively simple for its difficulty though it gets more complex in the second half with asymmetrical duals.
A slow and peaceful minimalistic level themed around a set of ruins that was impressively built in only 2 hours. Features precision timing gameplay throughout, with lots of corner block jumps.

A popular beginner solo extreme with colorful glow decoration throughout and a very repetitive song. Features fast-paced, clicksync gameplay with a mixture of gamemodes. Watch out for skipping any orbs, as the level gets angry at you if you do.

The oldest rated extreme demon. Used to be impossible due to an update turning a solid block into a decoration piece, until that was fixed, and the level was rated. Consists of one of the first instances of the swing copter, and some extremely hard ship parts. Generally poorly received, and is not recommended as a first extreme due to its extremely unbalanced, ending carried gameplay.

A short, skill-based level made using just three randomly generated colors. The gameplay is straightforward given its easier nature, but it spikes in difficulty with the ship and wave parts towards the second half of the level. rauchkammer is not advised to be beaten as a first extreme, as its gameplay is catered more towards skilled extreme grinders rather than new players.

A slow-paced, atmospheric insane demon with a winter theming that's captured by its song and decoration. The gameplay later on in the level is much more difficult compared to the first third of it, as the final wave and cube sections feature very tight gaps. The last click is especially difficult.
Miku level
Unique memory level where the gameplay on the top and bottom half is the same but offset by five blocks.
One of the only former extreme demons in which the main skillset is Spider. Very fast paced and flowy, which to some can be very fun, or very unfun.
